original_question: If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field, must any two quaternion division algebras over F that have the same finite splitting fields, or even just the same maximal subfields, already be isomorphic?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it has the correct field class, the correct objects (quaternion division algebras over F), the correct comparison conditions (same finite splitting fields, or even same maximal subfields), and the correct desired conclusion (isomorphism).
missing_details: State explicitly that the algebras are quaternion division F-algebras, i.e. central division F-algebras of degree 2.
Specify the quantifiers: for every field F finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field, and for every pair D, D' of quaternion division algebras over F.
Define 'same finite splitting fields' as: for every finite field extension E/F, D⊗F E is split if and only if D'⊗F E is split.
Clarify that 'finite' means finite field extensions of F, not finite-cardinality fields.
Define 'same maximal subfields' as: every maximal subfield of D admits an F-embedding into D', and every maximal subfield of D' admits an F-embedding into D.
Specify that the conclusion is 'isomorphic as F-algebras'.
Note that in the paper the maximal-subfields clause is presented as an even stronger version of the same question, not as a separate broader variant.
refined_question: Let F be a field finitely generated over either a prime field or an algebraically closed field, and let D and D' be quaternion division F-algebras. Suppose that D and D' have the same finite splitting fields, in the sense that for every finite field extension E/F, the algebra D⊗F E is split if and only if D'⊗F E is split. Must D and D' be isomorphic as F-algebras? Even more strongly, does the same conclusion already follow under the stronger hypothesis that D and D' have the same maximal subfields (i.e. every maximal subfield of one embeds over F into the other, and vice versa)?
justification: This is essentially Problem 10.5 verbatim. The surrounding discussion in §10 first recalls Amitsur’s theorem that all splitting fields almost determine a central simple algebra up to Brauer-theoretic ambiguity (Theorem 10.1), then asks finer questions for smaller classes of splitting fields (Problems 10.3 and 10.4), and finally specializes to quaternion division algebras over finitely generated fields in Problem 10.5. The sentence immediately preceding Problem 10.5 explains the quaternion/global-field motivation, and the paragraph immediately following it lists the relevant partial results of Garibaldi–Saltman, Rapinchuk–Rapinchuk, and Krashen–McKinnie. So your draft is targeting Problem 10.5, not the broader Amitsur conjecture (Conjecture 10.2) and not the higher-degree finiteness question in Problem 10.6.
